title: Jason Calacanis on angel investing: venture as jet fuel, portfolio math, and founder grit
summary: Jason explains how venture investing works: it's rocket fuel for outlier companies, most fail, and winners are unpredictable, so you place many bets and support every founder. He also covers leadership under chaos, knowing your superpower, and why podcasts are displacing journalism.

principles.text: Venture capital is rocket fuel for outlier companies; it doesn't suit normal small businesses.
principles.quote: venture capital is like jet fuel it's 40 or rocket fuel you wouldn't put rocket fuel like on a Vespa would not work out well

principles.text: Venture returns are a power law: most bets go to zero, and a rare winner returns 30x or more.
principles.quote: six are going to zero the seventh and eighth will return half the amount of money you put into them the ninth will return two or three times

principles.text: Nobody can pick winners in advance, so place many bets and treat every portfolio founder as a winner.
principles.quote: you just don't know which ones are gonna win so you just basically treat everybody who's in your portfolio amazing you try to just be as supportive as possible

principles.text: Define the goal, the plan, and who executes it; leaders stay calm and block out non-essentials in chaos.
principles.quote: what's the goal here what's the plan and who's going to execute the plan

principles.text: Founder success comes from self-possession and persistence, not a particular archetype; fill skill gaps with team members.
principles.quote: the founders that succeed most often are the ones who are self possessed and don't give up

principles.text: Know your superpower and lean into it; Jason's is talking, so he runs a podcast and invests in founders.
principles.quote: it's very important for you to understand what your skillset is what your personality is what you enjoy and then lean into that
